subject: Culture
title: Food Diplomacy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Food Diplomacy.

hook.text: Nixon ate Peking duck with Mao in 1972. That meal helped reopen US-China relations.

buildup.text: State dinners are strategic. The menu is a diplomatic signal—chosen to honor, impress, or provoke.

discovery.text: South Korea uses 'gastrodiplomacy'—promoting Korean food abroad to build cultural soft power.

twist.text: Thailand's 'Global Thai' program put Thai restaurants worldwide. Food exports more culture than embassies.

climax.text: A well-chosen meal can open negotiations that speeches cannot. Food disarms before words begin.

punchline.text: The table is the oldest negotiation room.

quiz.question: What is 'gastrodiplomacy'?
options: Using food promotion to build soft power
